evals.prompt: We want our Okta logs in Ingext. I'm an Okta super admin and I'm at the console now — walk me through whatever you need, then hook it up on the Fluency side yourself.
evals.expected_output: The skill takes the guided + agent-installs path: it recommends a dedicated service account with the Read-Only Administrator role as the token owner (explaining that Okta API tokens inherit the creator's permissions and die with the account), walks the admin through Security → API → Tokens → Create token, warns the value is shown once, and collects the org domain while flagging the '-admin' console-domain gotcha. It then installs the connector itself via the Fluency MCP: fetches the live Okta template with list_connector_templates, checks list_connectors for an existing instance, and calls create_connector with domain and token plus the defaulted datalake/index parameters, instance id 'okta' (never 'default'). It verifies with list_connectors and sets the 15–30 minute first-event expectation.
expectations: The skill guides the Okta portal steps but performs the Fluency-side install itself rather than handing over instructions
It recommends a least-privilege token owner (dedicated service account, Read-Only Administrator) and explains that the token inherits the owner's permissions
It warns the token value is shown once and that tokens expire after 30 days of non-use
It collects the bare org domain and flags that the -admin console domain must not be used
It fetches the live template schema and includes every template parameter in create_connector, with instance id derived from the template name and never 'default'
It never echoes the API token back in summaries or output

evals.prompt: Our customer's Okta admin isn't available today, but we want to get everything ready for them to connect Okta to Fluency. What do they need to do?
evals.expected_output: The skill selects the runbook-only path: it prints the complete Okta-side procedure for the absent admin — create/choose a least-privilege token owner (service account with Read-Only Administrator suggested), confirm that account can view Reports → System Log, create a token named ingext-okta under Security → API → Tokens, copy the value immediately, and note the org domain without the -admin part — and lists exactly what to send back: the domain and the token, with the token handled as a secret. It offers to run the Fluency-side connector install as soon as those two values return, and does not attempt to create anything now.
expectations: The skill recognizes the admin is absent and produces a complete vendor-side runbook instead of trying to act
The runbook covers token-owner choice, System Log visibility check, token creation path, the copy-once warning, and the org domain
It clearly states the two values to report back (domain, token) and that the token is a credential
It defers the Fluency-side install until the values arrive and offers to perform it then

evals.prompt: Add Okta to Ingext. Domain is acme.okta.com and the API token is 00abc...xyz — go.
evals.expected_output: Since both values are already in hand, the skill skips the Okta-side walkthrough and goes straight to the install: list_connector_templates for the live Okta schema, list_connectors to check for an existing instance (asking before creating a second one if present), then create_connector with application Okta, instance 'okta', displayName 'Okta Events', and the full parameter set including the defaulted datalake/index. It confirms the install, refers to the token only descriptively (never echoing it), reports the datalake index Okta for verification, and states the 15–30 minute first-event window before any row-count check.
expectations: The skill does not re-run the vendor-side walkthrough when domain and token are already provided
It checks for an existing Okta connector before installing and asks before creating a duplicate
create_connector includes every template parameter with defaults applied, instance id 'okta' rather than 'default'
The token is not repeated back in any confirmation or summary
It sets an honest first-event latency expectation before verifying row counts

evals.prompt: [Invoked from customer-onboarding] The customer picked Okta from the onboarding menu. The Fluency MCP is connected; the router's list_connectors call shows no Okta connector. The operator has an Okta admin on the call. Complete this stage and hand back to the onboarding checklist.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes the onboarding hand-off: it is self-contained, so it guides the token creation and performs create_connector itself WITHOUT chaining into add-connector and without re-collecting context the router already has. On return it hands the router the connector instance id and the Okta datalake index (confirming the live table name with list_data_tables before any query), keeps the API token out of the summary, and tells the router to expect first events within roughly 15–30 minutes — mark the application pending inside that window rather than failed.
expectations: The skill completes the connector creation itself and does not hand off to add-connector
It does not re-collect context the onboarding router already established
It hands back the instance id and datalake index for the router's verification step
The API token does not appear in the hand-back summary
It tells the router to mark the source pending within the 15–30 minute first-event window rather than failed
